title: M5 Ultra Chip's Impressive Performance Boost Revealed in First Benchmark Result
excerpt: The first unverified benchmark result for Apple's new M5 Ultra chip surfaced in the Geekbench 7 database today, offering a look at the chip's...
content_html:
Tuesday September 15, 2026 11:00 am PDT by Joe Rossignol

The first unverified benchmark result for Apple's new M5 Ultra chip surfaced in the Geekbench 7 database today, offering a look at the chip's impressive performance gains. The new Mac Studio will be Apple's first device to be equipped with the M5 Ultra.


Here is how the highest-end M5 Ultra chip with a 36-core CPU scored:

  • Single-core CPU score: 3,774
  • Multi-core CPU score: 52,516

Apple never released an M4 Ultra chip. Here are the average scores for the highest-end M3 Ultra chip with a 32-core CPU on Geekbench 7:

  • Single-core CPU score: 2,920
  • Multi-core CPU score: 39,059

Unsurprisingly, the M5 Ultra is Apple's fastest chip ever. If this Geekbench result is accurate, it has up to around 30% faster single-core CPU performance and up to around 35% faster multi-core performance compared to the M3 Ultra. But, it comes at a steep cost. In the U.S., the Mac Studio with a 36-core M5 Ultra starts at $6,799.

Apple said the M5 Ultra has up to 1.25× faster single-threaded CPU performance and up to 1.3× faster multi-threaded CPU performance compared to the M3 Ultra, so the benchmark result roughly aligns with or even beats those advertised claims. However, keep in mind that there wil be some variance in scores as additional results surface.

Here is where the M5 Ultra slots in for maximum multi-core CPU performance:

  • M5 Ultra: 52,516
  • M3 Ultra: 39,059
  • M5 Max: 35,119
  • M5 Pro: 33,593
  • M4 Max: 29,047
  • M2 Ultra: 28,789
  • M4 Pro: 24,894
  • M3 Max: 24,649
  • M1 Ultra: 23,328
  • M6: 22,783
  • M5: 17,948
  • M2 Max: 17,387
  • M3 Pro: 16,880
  • M2 Pro: 16,725
  • M4: 15,477
  • M1 Max: 14,299
  • M1 Pro: 13,914
  • M3: 11,650
  • M2: 9,809
  • M1: 8,582

Based on these scores, the M5 Ultra is up to 2.25× faster than Apple's original M1 Ultra chip and up to 6× faster compared to the regular M1 chip.

As always, real-world performance varies.

The new Mac Studio with M5 Max and M5 Ultra chips and the new Mac mini with M6 and M5 Pro chips launch on Tuesday, September 22.

We are still waiting for GPU results for the M5 Ultra to appear in the Geekbench 7 database.
